title: Nothing on a cruise brochure is free
subtitle: Free airfare, free drinks, free second guest. Each of them is priced into the fare.

text: A perk is not a gift. It is a fare with the discount pointed somewhere.
sub: Lines would rather add than subtract, because a perk sounds generous and a lower fare sounds like weak demand. Both come out of the same margin.

items.head: Free airfare
items.body: The line's routing, its airline, its connections. Ask what a deviation costs before you value it at full price.

items.head: Second guest sails free
items.body: Look at the total for two, not the headline. The fare for guest one has often been rebuilt to carry both.

items.head: Free drinks package
items.body: Worth real money to some travellers and nothing to others. It is only a saving at your own drinking pattern.

kicker: Two ways to be sold to
title: Perk or price

right.label: Price-led
items: Value is the same for all

quote: The useful question is never what am I getting. It's what would I have paid for this if it had a price on it.

text: Price the perks at what they are worth to you, then compare.
sub: Strike out every inclusion you wouldn't have bought. What remains is the real offer, and it is often a very different sailing that wins.

title: Which perk have you never once used
body: Tell me in the comments. Mine is the speciality dining credit that arrives on the night everyone is already booked.
